title: Separate pending byte pressure from drain readiness
summary: Separate autonomy pending-byte pressure from pending-publish drain readiness so high backlog size can warn or block new autonomous work without softlocking safe drain recovery.
reason: Pending byte thresholds are a new-work launch policy, not manifest drain-safety evidence. Treating aggregate byte pressure as a hard pending-drain blocker prevented operators from draining the parked files needed to reduce the backlog.
behavior_before: Autonomy pending-byte blockers could block drain_pending_pushes preflight/start and page-level pending health evidence could make otherwise safe drain rows look like Do-not-drain.
behavior_after: Normal queue/encode/autonomous starts still honor autonomy byte-pressure blocks, while pending-publish drain mode reports the pressure as review evidence and allows backend drain attempts for rows that pass manifest, payload, retry, sidecar, and path-safety readiness.
rollback_plan: Revert the pipeline/preflight autonomy drain-mode bypass, pending drain confidence classification changes, WebView summary classification changes, generated summaries, and the associated regression tests in this packet.
notes:
Allow pending-publish drain launch to bypass autonomy new-work byte pressure while preserving other launch guards.
Expose autonomy byte pressure as review evidence for drain mode instead of a hard preflight block.
Keep page-level health or byte-pressure evidence from turning otherwise safe drain rows into Do-not-drain.
Show pending health pressure as review evidence without disabling drain-ready rows.
Regress autonomy byte-pressure blocks normal starts but not pending-publish drain mode.
Regress high pending-byte/page-health pressure does not make safe manifests Do-not-drain.
Regress WebView drain guard allows safe rows while showing pending byte/health pressure as review.
Refresh generated summary for pending-publish recovery softlock fix.
